facts.claim: "LosT" is a song by the British rock band Bring Me the Horizon. It was released on 4 May 2023 as the third single from their seventh studio album Post Human: Nex Gen.
Zakk Cervini and Evil Twin produced the song. Wikipedia credits Cervini with production, mixing, mastering and programming.

Songfacts says Oli Sykes wrote the song with bandmates Matt Kean, Lee Malia, Matt Nicholls and Jordan Fish. Cervini and Evil Twin also worked on the band's "Strangers" and the Sigrid collaboration "Bad Life".
Shazam's credits list the writers as Jordan Fish, Lee Malia, Oliver Sykes and Zakk Cervini. This differs slightly from the Wikipedia and Songfacts lists.
NME describes the track as opening with a guitar fill over hyper-pop electronic production. The chorus has Sykes screaming about being "so terribly lost".

The song premiered as BBC Radio 1's Hottest Record on 4 May 2023. Sykes told Clara Amfo he was more excited to release it than "sTraNgeRs", and that it was the least excited he had been about releasing a song.
Sykes said "LosT" captures how he imagined the next record would sound. He called it "more honest" and likened it to "a therapy session with myself".
Songfacts reads the lyrics as covering Sykes' grief over his dog Oskar, who died on 26 April 2021. It also reads them as expressing disillusionment with therapy and medication.
The music video was released an hour after the single on 4 May 2023. Jensen Noen and Oli Sykes directed it.
Thomas Ian Nicholas, known as Kevin from American Pie, makes a cameo in the video. In it, three clones of Sykes lie on morgue trays.

research.lineage: Post Human: Nex Gen is a mainstream rock record that adds hyper-pop electronics to the band's sound. Sykes has said he wants the band to be "unhinged" and to reconnect with the period before they were big.

draft:
**LosT** opens on a scene that would be funny if it weren't so bleak: someone sprawled in front of Evangelion, high on ketamine, admitting they lost the plot a while ago. Then comes the inventory. The dog died. The friends are gone. There's a glimpse of themselves on MTV. And a line that rhymes like a joke and lands like a confession: "my ego is not my amigo." Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes has called the song "more honest" and likened it to "a therapy session with myself," and that's the right frame. It's a list of grievances that slowly turns into a diagnosis.

What makes it hit is how much the song refuses to choose between laughing and drowning. The verses joke about serotonin and imaginary enemies, but the humor is self-defense, and it cracks. "The next time that I open up to someone will be my autopsy" is a punchline about a therapist who tried to have the narrator sectioned, and it's also a promise never to trust anyone again. Bitterness and fear sit together, unresolved. The chorus drops the wit entirely. The medicine isn't working, there's no remedy, and the only question left is why. Songfacts reads the dead dog as Sykes' Oskar, who died in 2021, and reads the rest as disillusionment with therapy and medication. The most physical image is the smallest: "Red crescent moons all over my hands," nail marks from clenched fists, pain turned inward where nobody sees it.

The sound matches that pressure. The track starts with a melodic, slightly distorted vocal over a synth pad, then a distorted guitar riff and punchy drums crash in at a fast clip. The kick and snare sit right up front, and cymbal crashes mark the turns. The voice goes raw and strained, stacked with harmonies, while a bright synth line slips above the guitars. Zakk Cervini and Evil Twin produced it polished and wide, but the scream still sounds like it's coming apart at the seams. This is the third single from *Post Human: Nex Gen*, where the band bolts hyper-pop electronics onto big-room rock, and Sykes has said he wants them "unhinged" again, closer to the band before they got big. You can hear that here: glossy production around a person losing it.

Near the end, the lyrics shrink to a single warning, "If I keep this up" and the fear of breaking down, repeated until it sounds less like a threat than a forecast.

It sticks because it gives you a chorus you can shout along with about the exact thing you can't say out loud to anyone: that you've tried the fixes, and you still don't know what's wrong with you.

factCheck.claim: Opens on someone sprawled in front of Evangelion, high on ketamine, admitting they lost the plot a while ago.
factCheck.note: Lyrics support Evangelion, ketamine and 'lost the plot a little while ago.' 'Sprawled' is not in the lyrics, so it was removed.
The lyric is 'my friends hate me,' not that they are gone. Corrected.

factCheck.claim: The dog died; a glimpse of themselves on MTV.
factCheck.note: Matches 'My dog just died' and 'I saw myself on MTV.'

factCheck.claim: Oli Sykes has called the song "more honest" and likened it to "a therapy session with myself."
The verses joke about serotonin and imaginary enemies.
factCheck.note: Both appear in the lyrics. The 'joke' reading is interpretation.

factCheck.claim: "The next time that I open up to someone will be my autopsy" is a punchline about a therapist who tried to have the narrator sectioned.
factCheck.note: Quote is exact. The lyric says 'the doctor tried to section me,' so 'therapist' was changed to 'doctor.'

factCheck.claim: Songfacts reads the dead dog as Sykes' Oskar, who died in 2021, and the rest as disillusionment with therapy and medication.
factCheck.note: Oskar and the 2021 death are supported. The named attribution was reworded as a reading of the lyric, and the 'disillusionment' part stays as interpretation.

factCheck.claim: "Red crescent moons all over my hands"
factCheck.note: Exact lyric quote. 'Nail marks from clenched fists' is interpretation.

factCheck.claim: The track starts with a melodic, slightly distorted vocal over a synth pad.
factCheck.note: All three passes describe this, but 'starts' is a claim about position in the song. Reworded without placement.

factCheck.claim: A distorted guitar riff and punchy drums come in at a fast clip.
The kick and snare sit right up front, and cymbal crashes mark the turns.
factCheck.note: Prominent kick and snare are supported. Cymbal crashes are supported by two passes, but only one says they mark transitions, so that part was dropped.

factCheck.claim: The voice goes raw and strained, stacked with harmonies.
A bright synth line slips above the guitars.
factCheck.note: A synth melody above the guitars is supported by two passes. 'Bright' appears in only one, so it was removed.

factCheck.claim: Zakk Cervini and Evil Twin produced it, polished and wide.
factCheck.note: Production credit is supported. Polished and wide is supported by the passes.

factCheck.claim: Third single from Post Human: Nex Gen, where the band bolts hyper-pop electronics onto big-room rock.
factCheck.note: Third single and the hyper-pop electronics are supported. 'Big-room' is unsupported, and the record is described as mainstream rock.

factCheck.claim: Sykes has said he wants them "unhinged" again, closer to the band before they got big.
Near the end, the lyrics shrink to a single warning, 'If I keep this up'...
factCheck.note: The lyrics repeat this passage, but they do not show it is near the end; choruses follow it. Placement removed.

factCheck.claim: The scream still sounds like it's coming apart at the seams.
factCheck.note: Interpretation resting on the raw, strained vocal heard in the passes and NME's note that Sykes screams in the chorus.
